title: Study 5: what helps them work together (interventions, Claude with Claude)

variants.label: checker
roles: You write: draft the lines and fix them.

You check, in named passes, and say what you find in the chat with line numbers: (1) RULES: every rule, line by line, counting words and letters; (2) ASSUMPTIONS: what the writer assumed that the brief does not say; (3) READER: where someone hearing it aloud would stumble. You do not edit.

tasks.brief: Draw this scene on this 400 by 400 canvas: a lighthouse keeper’s cat watching a storm from the window. Use simple shapes (no text, letters or digits anywhere). Someone who knows nothing will be shown the picture and asked what it shows.
A twelve-line poem about two people repairing an old rowing boat together. Make it good enough to read aloud.

checks.say: Every line has exactly 8 words (a word is anything between spaces).
The first letters of the lines spell TOGETHERNESS, in order.
Every line names a colour: red, blue, green, gold, grey, white, black, silver or amber.
The last line ends with a question mark.
